Rental rules for a house with tenants

Owners of residential rentals must register each unit with the city and file interior and exterior inspection reports through an online portal every year, with a December 31 cutoff. Ordinance 8929, passed May 17, 2021, created the registration program, and the Planning Department runs it.

A registration stays valid until the owner, the use, or the contact information changes, which makes a sale a reportable event. An owner who lives more than 35 miles away must name a local agent who can accept service around the clock.

  • Landlords give each new occupant an information sheet that covers noise, alcohol, and nuisance-house rules.
  • A unit that falls out of self-certification needs an inspector approved by the city and registered with the Ohio Home Inspector Program.
  • An unregistered unit draws a penalty of $250 per week, and other violations start at $100.
  • Owner-occupied single-family homes where the occupants are the owner's family, and the owner's own unit in a two-family building, are exempt.

Before you list a rental, phone the Planning Department at (419) 354-6218. A buyer who wants to keep the tenants will ask for the registration and the last inspection forms, so pull those together early. Handing over the lease and deposit records at the same time makes the offer easier to price.

Deeds and property taxes in Wood County

Three Wood County offices touch your sale. The Auditor values the parcel and processes the deed transfer, the Recorder files the deed, and the Treasurer bills the tax. The Auditor's office answers at 419-354-9150.

The county's 2025 annual report shows the scale. Wood County had 74,320 parcels of real property valued at more than $4.3 billion, the Auditor processed 3,025 conveyances, and the Recorder filed 3,527 deeds. Some 7,290 residents were enrolled in the homestead exemption program. The Auditor's website carries online applications for that exemption and for the owner-occupancy tax reduction.

  • Fifteen area financial offices accept real estate tax payments.
  • Ohio's conveyance statute, Revised Code 319.202, puts the transfer fee on the seller.
  • Ask the Treasurer and your title company for the payoff through your closing date.

Repairs, disclosure and foreclosure

Most Ohio sellers of one to four unit homes fill out the state's condition disclosure form, found in Revised Code 5302.30. An heir who inherited the house and did not live there during the prior year is excluded from the requirement.

Foreclosure runs through Wood County's courts and sheriff. The 2025 county report lists 122 bank foreclosures and 36 sheriff foreclosure property sales. A homeowner who has received a foreclosure notice should ask the lender for a written payoff figure and talk to a title company about how a sale would close out the loan.

  • Collect any past-due tax notices and city letters about the property.
  • Photograph the repairs the house needs before you gather offers.
  • Compare each offer's closing costs line by line.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bowling Green houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Schools buyers ask about

The Bowling Green City School District runs Kenwood, Conneaut, and Crim elementary schools, plus the middle school and senior high school. Private options include Bowling Green Christian Academy, the Montessori School of Bowling Green, and St. Aloysius. The city sits about 20 miles southwest of Toledo, which suits buyers who commute.

Walk through the sale in order. Decide which path fits your timeline, gather the rental or tax paperwork, ask a title company for a payoff figure, and compare offers on net proceeds after closing costs rather than headline price. If the house has tenants, tell them early so showings do not catch anyone off guard, and keep copies of every notice you send. If a buyer asks for repairs after an inspection, you can answer, negotiate a credit, or walk away from that offer and take another.

Frequently asked questions

How soon can a sale close in Bowling Green?

The timeline follows the type of buyer. With cash there is no lender appraisal to wait on, so title work sets the pace. Financed buyers move at the lender's speed, so put the closing date in your signed contract.

Must I register a Bowling Green rental before I sell it?

If the unit is covered by Chapter 121, yes. The registration and yearly inspection forms belong to the property owner, and a change of ownership gets reported. The Planning Department at (419) 354-6218 can tell you whether your unit is exempt.

Who pays the transfer fee on a Wood County sale?

The seller does, under Revised Code 319.202. Once the buyer files a statement of value, the auditor stamps the deed. The settlement sheet from the title company shows the amount.

May I sell a Bowling Green house while a tenant lives in it?

Yes. Investors often like a house with income in place. Hand over the lease, the deposit records, and the city's rental registration and inspection history.

How do I dispute my Wood County property value?

Use the Board of Revision, which takes complaints through the Auditor's office. State law gives you until March 31 of the next tax year, or a later first-half collection close. Call 419-354-9150 for the form.

Quick-sale options in North Royalton

Selling here means choosing among a broker, a sale you run yourself, or a buyer paying cash who takes on the repairs. Every route finishes at one Cuyahoga County desk for transfer and recording, which leaves time and renovation effort as the real question. Landlords also owe the city a rental certificate on rented single, double and triple homes.

  • Pick a broker if the house is in good shape and you can live with tours and an inspection report.
  • Skipping the agent saves commission, but the contract and deed work lands on you and whoever handles closing.
  • Cash suits estate houses, long-deferred repairs, empty rentals and tight moving dates.

North Royalton housing profile

North Royalton is a suburb in southern Cuyahoga County covering 21.32 square miles, with 31,322 residents at the 2020 census. The mid-2025 estimate is 30,936. Growth has been slow, from 30,444 in 2010, so a listing here mostly competes with other established houses. Owners occupy about seven in ten homes, and more than nine in ten residents stayed put the year before.

The 2020 count found 14,125 housing units, 4.4% of them vacant.

Rental certificate and short-term rental limits

For a rented house, Chapter 1485 of the city ordinances calls for a Certificate of Rental Registration from the Building Commissioner before anyone moves in. File it by December 31 ahead of the year it covers, or within thirty days of the house first turning into a rental. It ends on December 31 of its year. Multi-unit owners must renew every year or file an exemption form.

Timing sets the fee. A single-family rental registered by February 1 pays $50, and one filed after March 1 pays $125. An exemption form costs nothing before February 1 and $50 afterward. Skipping registration is a first-degree misdemeanor under the chapter.

Nightly rentals are tightly limited. The chapter treats any stay under thirty consecutive days as short-term. Tenant-occupied units cannot host transient guests at all. Owner-occupants may host for at most fourteen days a year, must live in the home at least 351 days a year, and need a transient rental registration certificate. A buyer who counted on nightly rental income needs to hear this before bidding.

State law adds one more step on a rental sale: the county stamps the deed with a reminder that the incoming owner files owner information with the auditor under Ohio Revised Code 5323.02.

How a sale is recorded in Cuyahoga County

Transfers go through the county Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, which absorbed the earlier auditor, recorder and engineer offices. Real Estate Services requires one of two forms with every transfer: DTE 100, the value statement and receipt, or DTE 100-EX, which explains why no conveyance fee is owed.

Ohio Senate Bill 94 set the current recording fee on October 24, 2024: $39 covers two pages and every extra page is $8. Find the division on the fourth floor at 2079 E. Ninth Street in Cleveland. Weekday recording stops at 4 p.m. Staff may not offer legal advice, and drafting a deed counts as practicing law, so let a closing agent or lawyer prepare it.

Under section 5302.30 of the Ohio code, sellers hand buyers a property disclosure form promptly. Estate fiduciary transfers are among the exemptions.

Selling an inherited house

Inherited houses take special routes at the county. The conveyance standards describe an affidavit of real estate inherited under Ohio Revised Code 317.22, a probate court certificate of transfer, and a survivorship affidavit under 5302.17. A separate Great Estates Program page is aimed at families settling an estate.

The right paper depends on how title passed to you. Ask the probate court or your closing agent which one applies before you sign a contract. Once that document is recorded, the sale moves through the same steps as any other: contract, title work, deed, DTE form, recording.

From signed contract to recorded deed

The order of events is the same whichever route you pick. First the contract is signed and title work begins. If the house was a rental, the rental certificate and any county owner filing get sorted out. Next the disclosure form goes to the buyer, unless an exemption such as an estate fiduciary transfer applies. Then your closing agent or lawyer drafts the deed and fills in DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX. At closing the settlement agent divides the tax bill and pays off anything owed. Last, the deed and form go to the Fiscal Officer's division on East Ninth Street with the recording fee. Ask for a copy of each document so your own file is complete.

Tax bills and the Board of Revision

County real estate bills run a year behind, so what is payable in one calendar year covers the year before. Each bill is split into two halves, and an unpaid half picks up a 10 percent penalty. Phone the County Treasurer for this year's due dates instead of trusting an old calendar.

The settlement agent divides the current bill between you and the buyer and takes any past-due amount from your proceeds, so find out early what you owe. A value that seems too high can be challenged with the county Board of Revision, which accepts complaints yearly through March 31. A closing statement or DTE 100 counts as evidence. The board can also raise a value, so file only with solid numbers.

Is a cash buyer worth a call?

Usually the answer turns on time and condition. Cash buyers purchase as is, which removes contractors, showings and appraisal waits. That can help when an estate must wrap up, a rental has tenant trouble or a move has a firm date.

Insist on a written offer and measure it against a listing's take-home after commission and repairs. Settle who covers the recording fee, what the closing date is, and who deals with the rental certificate and the county owner filing if tenants lived there. Title work, the deed and the DTE form still apply to a cash sale, and a house with open rental paperwork needs that cleared first.

Frequently asked questions

Does a rented North Royalton house need a certificate?

Yes, if the house is a rental. Chapter 1485 bars anyone from occupying a residential rental unit unless a current Certificate of Rental Registration has been issued, and the certificate expires each December 31. Keep it current while tenants live there.

Where is a North Royalton deed filed?

At the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX attached. Recording costs $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page beyond that.

Are nightly rentals allowed in North Royalton?

Only in narrow cases. Owners living in the home 351 or more days a year may host guests up to fourteen days annually with a registration certificate. Tenant-occupied units may not host them.

What is the penalty on a late Cuyahoga County tax bill?

Ten percent is added to an unpaid half-year bill. Ask the Treasurer for the due dates that apply this year.

What if I inherited the North Royalton house?

Title reaches the heirs through a probate court certificate or an affidavit of real estate inherited, and the county lists both routes in its conveyance standards. An heir who did not live in the house within the past year is generally excused from the Ohio disclosure form, but should confirm with a closing agent.

Selling quickly in Marysville

In Marysville you may hire a broker, track down a buyer on your own, or accept a plain cash purchase. The route changes, but the deed paperwork still lands at the Union County auditor and recorder.

Match the house's condition to your calendar. Listing reaches the most buyers but adds showings and an inspection report. A cash offer leaves a single negotiation over price and closing day.

Marysville home values and households

Marysville has an estimated 30,190 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,571 in the April 2020 count. That is growth of 17.9 percent since the 2020 estimates base, and it has kept demand for houses steady.

The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $300,800 for 2020-2024, and owners live in 67.5 percent of units. Rent has a median of $1,223 a month, and owner costs have medians of $1,851 with a mortgage and $681 without one. The city has 10,163 households averaging 2.46 people, and median household income is $92,619.

Citywide medians say little about one address. Ask for a written review of recent sales near yours before you accept any number.

Why buyers choose Marysville

The Union County seat sits roughly 27 miles northwest of Columbus, and its employers keep a steady stream of buyers nearby. Scotts Miracle-Gro was founded here in 1868 and still has its headquarters in the city. Honda's Marysville Auto Plant, about six miles northwest, has built the Accord since 1982. Nestle, Univenture and a Parker Hannifin plant add more jobs.

U.S. Route 33 runs four lanes through town, tying it to Interstate 75 and the I-270 outerbelt. Tree-lined streets earned the city the nickname Shaded City, and more than 300 acres of parks hold trails along Mill Creek. The Union County Fair runs from late July into early August.

Timberview, an upscale section with a golf course, and Greenwood Colony sit on the south side, and the Uptown square holds the library and city offices.

Weather and an older house

Marysville gets 40.48 inches of precipitation and 24.0 inches of snow in a typical year. January lows average 20.6 degrees Fahrenheit, and the all-time record high is 109. Roofs, gutters, basements and furnaces absorb those swings each year, which is why an inspector looks at them first.

When one of those is nearly worn out, tell buyers at the start. Cash buyers simply price the work in; financed buyers bring it up after inspection.

School district and tax rate

Almost all of Marysville falls in the Marysville Exempted Village School District, with a few parcels reaching into Fairbanks Local. The district changes your tax bill, so verify it for the parcel.

The Union County auditor's GIS map includes a school district layer. If a district line cuts through a house, the district holding the master bedroom taxes the entire house. The auditor's parcel page has a "Where your taxes go" link that lists every levy and a Total Effective Rate, which is the quickest way to see the rate for your address.

What a Marysville seller must disclose

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 sets the disclosure duty for houses with up to four units. The seller completes the state form, signs and dates it, and hands it to prospective buyers. It asks about water supply, sewage, roof and foundation, radon, lead paint, asbestos and other known defects.

The duty does not reach every transfer. Excluded sales include:

  • Court-ordered transfers and fiduciary transfers for an estate or trust.
  • Transfers to a spouse or direct-line relatives.
  • Heirs who never lived in the house during the previous year.

A buyer handed the form late may cancel in writing for three business days after receiving it. That right lapses 30 days after acceptance or at closing, if sooner.

The auditor and recorder

Ohio Revised Code 5301.01 has the seller sign the deed and acknowledge it before a notary or similar officer. The deed then goes to the Union County Auditor at 233 W. Sixth St. in Marysville, where the buyer's side files a value statement (DTE 100) or an exemption statement (DTE 100EX).

The seller settles the conveyance fee, so ask the auditor which rate applies before closing day. Mailed conveyances reach the recorder only with the auditor's stamp already applied. The recorder charges $39.00 for a deed through page two, then $8.00 a page.

Appeals, exemptions and deadlines

A Board of Revision complaint on a Union County parcel must reach the auditor after January 1 and on or before March 31. The other deadlines and amounts are below.

  • The 2.5 percent rollback covers owner-occupied homes, one property per owner, and requires an application.
  • A requested change above $50,000 of market value, or $17,500 assessed, sends notice to the school board.
  • After a recent sale, attach the closing statement, contract and deed to support your complaint.

Permits for improvements

Marysville requires a zoning permit for most additions: decks, fences, swimming pools, sheds, garages and room additions, plus public sidewalks and driveway approaches built by a contractor registered with the city. Some jobs also need a building permit from the Union County Building Department.

Ask the city zoning office about any structure on your lot that lacks one. Old decks and sheds show up on inspections, and a cash buyer will price in whatever cleanup remains.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

When a cash sale fits

A cash sale suits owners who value a quick, certain close over the last few thousand dollars of price. Common cases:

  • An inherited house nobody plans to occupy.
  • An aging roof, furnace or foundation.
  • Tenants who make showings hard to schedule.
  • A job move on a fixed date.

Set any offer beside what a listing would leave you after repair bills, commission and months of upkeep. A cash buyer also skips the lender's appraisal, so a low appraisal cannot pull the price down late in the process.

Closing day in Marysville

Plan on three things in the last week: a signed and notarized deed, the value or exemption statement for the auditor, and a payoff letter if a mortgage remains. A title company can carry the deed to the Union County Auditor and then to the recorder, and it will list any taxes still owed on your settlement statement. Keep copies of the disclosure form and anything else you handed the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Marysville house without making repairs?

Yes. Ohio sets no repair requirement for a sale, but problems you know about belong on the disclosure form. A cash purchaser accepts the house as found, while a buyer with a lender may ask for fixes.

Who pays the conveyance fee on a Marysville sale?

The seller does. Under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 the grantor settles it before the auditor endorses the deed.

When can I challenge my Marysville property value?

Union County takes these complaints from January 1 to March 31, for the current tax year only. A notarized complaint goes to the auditor by email, fax or mail.

Does an inherited Marysville house need the disclosure form?

Frequently not. Transfers by an estate's fiduciary are excluded, as are sales by heirs who never occupied the house in the previous year.

How do I find the tax rate for a Marysville parcel?

Look up the parcel on the Union County auditor's website. The Total Effective Rate column under "Where your taxes go" gives the rate for that district.

Garfield Heights puts an inspection between the contract and the closing table. Sellers apply to the Building Department for a Certificate of Inspection, and the city issues a Compliance Certificate that the buyer needs for title transfer.

The city sits in Cuyahoga County, borders Cleveland, covers 7.23 square miles of land, and uses ZIP codes 44105, 44125 and 44128. Home values are low by regional standards: the median owner-occupied home is $109,900, and 58.5 percent of households own. Median gross rent is $1,129 and median household income is $54,593. Population is 28,790 for 2025, down from 29,781 in 2020, so buyers have choices and condition matters.

The point-of-sale inspection

Chapter 1313 of the codified ordinances applies before any sale, transfer or agreement to sell. The buyer must be shown a Certificate of Inspection, or a Certificate of Compliance dated within a year before the agreement. The city's inspection page and the ordinance set out the steps:

  • The owner or an agent applies on the Building Commissioner's form, and the inspection happens within ten days after the application and fee are received.
  • The certificate follows within ten working days after the inspector gains access and lists code violations found, which the owner must correct within 90 days unless the commissioner extends the time for good cause.
  • The fee is $200 for a dwelling and $300 for a commercial building. Each re-inspection after the first two costs $35, and a missed appointment without one business day of notice costs $25.
  • The buyer signs an acknowledgment of receiving the certificate, and a copy goes to the Building Department as a condition of transferring title.
  • If violations remain at closing, escrow of at least $100 and equal to 110 percent of the higher of two written repair estimates is required, or an approved bond.

The ordinance doesn't apply to a transfer by inheritance or gift where no real sale is intended. Escrow agents may not transfer title or release funds until the chapter has been satisfied, so file the application early, before an offer is in hand.

Documents the buyer signs

The city requires a notarized Buyer's Acknowledgement Form, returned in original to the office. A business buyer must designate an agent, and an out-of-state business must register with the Ohio Secretary of State as a foreign corporation before the Compliance Certificate is issued.

If the buyer is assuming outstanding violations, a notarized Affidavit is also needed, and the buyer has 90 days from the transfer date to finish the repairs. The seller's signature on the affidavit isn't required for bank-owned, Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac properties. The city also offers separate forms for individuals and businesses, a consent form for an interior inspection, and a snow-covered-property agreement.

The Building and Housing office is at 5407 Turney Road, 2nd floor, open weekdays until 3:45 p.m. Send applications by email to buildingdept@garfieldhts.org or by fax. Emails are processed within two business days, and fees increased in 2025.

Recording and transfer in Cuyahoga County

One Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office division took over what the auditor, recorder and engineer used to do, at 2079 E. Ninth Street, 4th floor, Cleveland. Each transfer must carry a DTE 100 value statement or a DTE 100-EX exemption statement.

Ask the Fiscal Office for the conveyance fee that applies to your sale. Drafting a deed is the practice of law under Ohio Supreme Court rulings, so county staff won't advise you. Owners may draft their own.

Selling a Garfield Heights house with violations

Because of the inspection rule, speed depends on who handles the violations.

  • Agent listing: the buyer sees the certificate up front, and you fix cited items inside 90 days or fund the escrow.
  • Sale as-is to an investor: the buyer can assume violations through the affidavit and finish repairs within 90 days of transfer.
  • Inherited property: a transfer by inheritance or gift without a bona fide sale falls outside the point-of-sale chapter.

The Building and Housing page also links a Cuyahoga County list of homes scheduled for demolition, which requires notice to lien holders first. Ask the department how a long violation list could affect your house.

Neighborhood points buyers ask about

The Dan Kostel Recreation Center on Turney Road has an outdoor summer pool and an indoor ice rink, and the Garfield Park Reservation, part of Cleveland Metroparks, sits in the northeast corner on the Cleveland border. The Wargo Farms parcel, about 45 acres, was sold to Cleveland Metroparks in 2023 for green space and trails. The Highland Park development, built on a former landfill and bought out of receivership in 2020, has added employers such as MPAC Switchback, MTech, Innoplast and Thermoprene.

The Garfield Heights school system runs three elementary schools, one middle school and Garfield Heights High School. Mention parks and the nearby jobs in a listing, since they answer the first questions buyers ask.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Garfield Heights houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

From offer to closing in Garfield Heights

Apply for the inspection as soon as you decide to sell. Once you have a contract, the buyer signs the acknowledgment, the certificate goes to the Building Department, and the title company confirms the chapter has been satisfied. Only then can the escrow agent transfer title or release funds.

The deed goes to the Fiscal Office with a DTE form, and recording follows. Bring photo identification and any mortgage payoff letter to the signing, and the notarized affidavit if the buyer is assuming violations. For a business buyer, check early that its agent is designated and its registration is in order, since the Compliance Certificate waits on both.

A cash buyer will often take a house with open violations, which means the affidavit and the 90-day repair clock rather than an escrow holdback from your proceeds. Ask for each offer in writing, with the price, closing date and who pays each fee, and compare what you net after fees, any tax proration and loan payoff. If you can't tell whether a transfer qualifies as a gift or inheritance, call the Building Department before you sign anything.

Frequently asked questions

Does Garfield Heights make sellers get an inspection first?

Yes. Chapter 1313 ties a sale to a Certificate of Inspection, and the buyer then needs a Compliance Certificate to take title. The dwelling fee is $200 under the 2024 ordinance.

What is the deadline to correct cited violations?

Ninety days from the certificate, unless the Building Commissioner extends it for good cause. A buyer who assumes the violations by affidavit gets 90 days from the transfer date.

Can I sell if I cannot pay for repairs before closing?

Yes, with escrow or a bond. The escrow runs at least $100 and equals 110 percent of the higher of two written estimates. A buyer who signs the affidavit can also take the house with violations open.

Which office files the deed after a Garfield Heights closing?

The Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office, in its Transfer and Recording division at 2079 E. Ninth Street. The deed travels with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX, and recording starts at $39 for two pages.

Does an inherited Garfield Heights house skip the inspection?

Only when it passes by inheritance or gift with no real sale intended. Listing the inherited house for sale brings the chapter back into play, so call the Building Department first.

Selling in Shaker Heights starts with an inspection

Shaker Heights is a planned inner-ring suburb on Cleveland's eastern edge, and a sale here starts with a city inspection that most Ohio towns do not require. The Point of Sale rule covers every residential sale, so how fast you can sell depends on how soon the inspection can be booked.

Population is 28,466 by the July 2025 estimate, down 3.4% from the April 2020 base, on 6.29 square miles of land. Houses sit close together and many were built in the first half of the twentieth century. Roughly 75 percent of the city's area lies inside the Shaker Village Historic District, a federal historic listing. The city holds houses to its own maintenance chapters in the codified ordinances: Chapter 1411 for residential occupancy and Chapter 1412 for landscaping and yard upkeep.

Typical home value is $303,200, 60.3% of households own, and there are 12,806 households in all. Rent at the midpoint is $1,168 a month.

Point of Sale inspection and who pays

It is a visual interior and exterior inspection the seller must schedule through the city before signing a contract with a buyer, and the seller pays the fee. The application goes in online through the city's CitizenServe system, with payment taken in the same step.

An inspector walks the house, the garage and the yard. For a single or two family home the visit takes about 90 minutes. The city asks sellers to allow at least two weeks from application, and three to four weeks in the busy spring season, so applying before you list is the practical move.

The Building and Housing Department is at 3400 Lee Road, phone 216-491-1460, with in-person counter service weekdays between 8:30 and 3:30 and phone or email contact until 5 p.m. Permit, license and Point of Sale applications are online only.

What happens if the inspector finds violations?

You get a Certificate of Inspection listing what must be fixed, and you have 90 days to correct the items and book a re-inspection whether or not the house sells. A house with no violations receives a Certificate of Compliance instead, and the property can transfer within 24 months of that first inspection.

If repairs will still be open at closing, the buyer or seller submits an itemized estimate prepared by a registered contractor. The buyer then funds an escrow account at 150 percent of the estimated repair cost, held by the city. The city also reviews requests to swap the escrow for a purchase rehab loan when the buyer will live in the home, and it names the HUD 203(K) program as one example of such a loan.

  • The city grants extensions of the 90-day period when repairs are progressing but unfinished, especially where weather is a factor.
  • A buyer who takes a property at sheriff's sale or another court-ordered auction has 30 days after transfer to obtain the inspection.
  • Violations you dispute or do not understand can be raised with the department, which answers questions on deadlines, extensions and affordability.

Other city inspections on a Shaker Heights house

Beyond the sale inspection, the city runs a standing cycle. Owner-occupied homes receive an exterior review every five years, and rental properties get an interior and exterior inspection every three years. Neighbor complaints trigger their own inspection, and any violation notice carries a compliance deadline.

An older violation notice may already be on file for your address. Ask the Building and Housing Department whether anything is open before you sign a listing agreement or accept an offer.

What buyers look for

Buyers here shop by neighborhood. There are nine, each named after one of the original elementary schools: Boulevard, Fernway, Lomond, Ludlow, Malvern, Mercer, Moreland, Onaway and Sussex. Public school students attend the Shaker Heights City School District. Two Greater Cleveland Regional Transit Authority rail lines end in the city: the Blue Line runs down the median of Van Aken Boulevard and the Green Line down the median of Shaker Boulevard. Houses within walking range of a station and a neighborhood school often draw the most interest, so mention both in a listing.

Property taxes when a house sells

Cuyahoga County bills the tax, and the Fiscal Office handles valuation and the Homestead program. Ask the Cuyahoga County Treasurer for the schedule on your parcel so the title company can prorate the bill to the closing date.

The Homestead exemption is open to owners aged 65 and up, those permanently and totally disabled, and certain surviving spouses, with an income limit of $41,000 for the current application and $29,000 of value exempted. The applicant must own and occupy the home on January 1, and the filing deadline is December 31. If the owner sells, the exemption stays with the house for that tax year, but a recipient who buys another home must file again. Taxes and the Homestead program run through the county Fiscal Office at 2079 East Ninth Street in Cleveland, and Homestead questions go to 216-443-7420, option 5.

Where to go for each step

Two offices carry most of the work: the city for the inspection and the county for taxes. Start with the city, because the inspection controls the contract date. Book the Point of Sale application first, then call the Building and Housing Department about any open notice, and only after that line up the county tax questions with the title company. Keep the certificate the city issues, because a buyer or lender will ask to see it.

When a cash offer makes sense

A cash offer makes sense when the house carries open violations you do not want to repair before closing. The city allows the buyer to take on all or part of the repair responsibility, so a direct buyer can purchase as is and set up the escrow for the remaining items.

That arrangement still runs through the city. The inspection must be applied for before the contract is signed, the escrow still equals 150 percent of the contractor estimate, and the buyer holds the repair duty after title passes. Compare at least two offers, ask who covers the inspection fee and escrow, and get the closing date in writing before you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an inspection to sell my house in Shaker Heights?

Yes. The city requires a Point of Sale inspection for residential sales, and the application must be filed before you enter into a contract with a buyer. The fee is $200 for a single-family home.

How long does a Shaker Heights Point of Sale inspection take to schedule?

Plan on at least two weeks from the application date, and three to four weeks in the spring season. The visit itself takes about 90 minutes for a single or two family home.

What is the difference between a Certificate of Compliance and a Certificate of Inspection?

A Certificate of Compliance means the house passed and can transfer within 24 months. A Certificate of Inspection means violations were found and must be fixed within 90 days, even if the house is not sold.

Can a buyer take a Shaker Heights house with violations still open?

Yes, with an itemized contractor estimate and an escrow account for 150 percent of the repair cost. For owner-occupant buyers, the city may accept a purchase rehab loan in place of the escrow.

Who do I ask about property tax on a Shaker Heights sale?

Ask the Cuyahoga County Treasurer and Fiscal Office. They can confirm the due dates on your parcel and any Homestead credit, so the title company prorates the bill correctly at closing.

Should a Kent owner list, sell alone or take cash?

A Kent seller has three routes: hire a listing agent, run the sale personally, or sell to a company that closes with its own money and no mortgage underwriting. The choice turns on the house itself, any tenants and your calendar.

  • Listing agent: works for a clean, updated house when weeks of showings and a loan approval are acceptable.

Just 40.8 percent of Kent households own their home. Much of what trades hands near campus is former student housing or small rentals, so buyers raise leases, inspections and licenses early.

The university and the housing stock

Kent State University employs more people than anyone else here, and its 866 acre main campus on the southeast side shapes demand for houses within walking distance. The compact city covers 9.22 square miles of land, with older frame houses near downtown and campus and postwar blocks farther out. Public and private spending of about $110 million has gone into downtown projects such as Acorn Alley, a hotel and the Kent Central Gateway transit garage.

  • Schools: the Kent City School District covers most addresses, with Stanton Middle School and Theodore Roosevelt High School. The part of Kent south of State Route 261 belongs to the Field Local School District, so check which one serves a house before you advertise it.
  • Getting around: State Route 59 follows Main Street across downtown, State Route 43 carries traffic north and south, and Interstate 76 is about 3 miles south by way of exit 33. The PARTA bus system links Kent with Akron and Cleveland.

Which Kent offices to contact before closing

Start with the Building Division at 930 Overholt Road, phone 330-678-8107, which handles permits and the city's Exterior Maintenance Code. Ask whether any permit on your address was never closed out, because unfinished work can hold up a closing.

  • Rentals with four or more unrelated tenants: the Kent City Health Department, at 201 E. Erie Street, second floor, phone 330-678-8109, licenses these multiple use dwellings and investigates housing maintenance complaints under the city's Environmental Health and Housing Maintenance Code.
  • One and two family rentals: these get their license from the Community Development Department, which can be reached at 330-678-8108. For code issues at unlicensed homes and small rentals, the city lists 330-678-8464.

With tenants in place, tell the buyer which license applies and keep a copy for the closing file.

Deed transfer in Portage County

Portage County's Auditor runs the transfer step for Kent, the county's largest city. The Auditor's Real Estate Department handles each deed ahead of recording. The fee is $4.00 per $1,000.00 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel, and the Auditor's page links the DTE 100 form.

Transfers by an estate fiduciary, and a sale to someone who has already occupied the home for twelve months, appear among the exceptions. A buyer who never gets the form can back out, within a window that ends no later than closing.

Selling as is does not remove the duty. A lower price leaves you answering the form in good faith, so fill it out with what you actually know and keep a signed copy.

Is a cash buyer a good fit for a worn or tenant occupied Kent house?

Cash is worth a look when certainty outranks the top price. Kent examples include a rental whose lease has months left, repairs that would stall a lender's appraisal, or a vacant house left behind by an estate.

Get any offer on paper, with the closing date, the party paying title and recording costs, and the buyer's rule if a walkthrough finds something new. Set two or three offers beside the net an agent would deliver after commission and repairs, and ask the Portage County Auditor what conveyance charge applies so the settlement sheet holds no surprises. Kent's low owner rate means many buyers are investors, so the offers you see may come from landlords who will want the existing lease, the license and the rent roll handed over at closing.

Selling a Kent rental with tenants

Student rentals have their own rhythm, so plan around the lease.

  2. Decide whether to sell to a buyer who takes over the tenancy or to time closing around move out.
  3. Confirm which license covers the rental: the Health Department for four or more unrelated tenants, Community Development for one and two family rentals.
  4. Hand the buyer copies of the lease and the license.
  5. Ask the Building Division whether any permit remains open.

A cash buyer will often take a tenant-occupied house as is, which spares you the cost of emptying and repairing a house just to list it.

Can I sell a Kent house with student tenants still inside?

Yes. Read the lease for its end date, then either sell to a buyer who takes over the tenancy or plan the closing around move out. Confirm which Kent license covers the rental and hand the buyer copies of the lease and license.

Who collects the transfer fee when a house sells in Kent?

The Portage County Auditor collects it, and the city does not. The Auditor's page lists $4.00 per $1,000.00 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel, and Ohio Revised Code 319.202 places the fee on the grantor.

Does selling my Kent home as is skip the disclosure form?

Usually no. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 reaches one to four unit residential property, and a discounted as is price leaves the duty to complete the form in good faith untouched. Estate fiduciary sales and the other listed transfers are exempt.

Which school district does my Kent house belong to?

Most of Kent is in the Kent City School District, but addresses south of State Route 261 are in the Field Local School District. Ask the district or the county before you put a district name in a listing.

How can I find out what my Kent house is worth?

Search the parcel on the Portage County Auditor's property records for valuation and sales history, then compare an agent's opinion with written cash offers. The county figure serves tax purposes and often differs from a market price.

What does the Summit County Fiscal Office charge to transfer a Green deed?

One drafting rule catches people. When a survey was made of the land being conveyed, the surveyor's name has to appear in the deed, and the county auditor can insist on it. If you have a survey from your purchase, hand it to the title company early so the description is drafted right the first time. A seller who skips this step can see closing slip a few days while the deed is redrafted.

Most sellers never carry the deed in. A title company or closing agent normally prepares it, files the transfer forms and pays the fees from your proceeds.

Pipelines, easements and older parcels

Green fought the NEXUS Pipeline in court starting in 2016 because the line runs near residential neighborhoods, wetlands and the Comet Lake Dam. Construction began in 2018 after the city reached a $7.5 million settlement. If your lot is near the route, check your title paperwork for any easement before a buyer asks.

From about 1950, farmers began selling land to developers, so Green houses range from older farm properties to newer subdivision homes. An older house with an original well, septic system or outbuildings will draw different questions from an inspector than a recent subdivision home.

  • Agent listing: a fit for move-in-ready homes where recent nearby sales give a clear price.
  • Investor sale: suited to dated houses, open code complaints, or an estate sale on a deadline.
  • Owner sale: saves commission but requires you to prepare the DTE 100 and deed paperwork.
  • Sale to a relative or neighbor: the exemption form may apply, and the 50 cent lot fee is owed either way.

Whichever route you pick, price the house against nearby Green sales and check for open zoning complaints.

Steps from decision to closing

A cash sale skips the weeks of showings and lender appraisal, but the paperwork is the same, so it helps to know the order.

  1. Confirm the parcel is inside Green and note the school district.
  2. Call the Zoning Division about open complaints and fix the visible ones.
  3. Gather the survey and title papers, plus any septic records.
  4. Choose a route and compare each written offer by what you would keep after repairs and holding costs.
  5. Have the title company prepare the deed and the DTE 100, with the full consideration stated.
  6. Pay the conveyance fee and the 50 cent lot charge at closing, and let the Recording Division file the deed.

If the buyer is a relative, ask the Fiscal Office whether the DTE 100(EX) exemption form applies before closing day.

Bring a few things to the title company: a photo ID, the survey if you have one, any easement or septic papers, and the loan payoff details if a mortgage remains. The mortgage or lien balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, and the buyer's side confirms the numbers on the statement of value match the contract.

Who issues permits for a house in Green?

The city's Zoning Division handles zoning permits and inspections of new structures. The Summit County Department of Building Standards is the county agency for building permits.

How much is the Summit County conveyance fee on a Green sale?

The fee is $4.00 per $1,000, with the price rounded up to the next $100, plus 50 cents per lot. Forms in by 3:30 p.m. get same-day legal description approval.

Where does a Green deed get recorded?

In Akron, at the Fiscal Office Recording Division on South Main Street. Ohio records a deed in the county where the land sits.

Is my Green house inside the city limits?

Not always, since some ZIP codes are shared with neighboring places. Ask the Summit County Fiscal Office to confirm your parcel.

How do I find out about code complaints on my Green house?

Call the Zoning Division at 330-896-6605. Overgrown grass, junk vehicles, stored RVs and general disrepair top its list of violations.

Selling fast in Troy without months of showings

Troy sellers who want speed have two main choices: an as-is cash purchase, or a listing priced to move. The right one follows the house. A downtown address inside the Historic District raises different questions than a recent subdivision home, so figure out where yours stands first.

  • Agent listing: reaches Dayton-area buyers, with an inspection and loan approval still ahead of closing.
  • Owner-handled sale: you draft the contract, deliver the disclosure form and arrange the deed.
  • Direct as-is purchase: the buyer takes on the repairs, and you set closing to fit your move.

The finish is the same on every route. The deed clears the Miami County Engineer and Auditor, then goes to the Recorder.

Troy market snapshot

Troy is the Miami County seat and its largest city, on the Great Miami River about 19 miles north of Dayton. It's growing: the estimate is 27,344 residents, up 3.8 percent from the April 2020 base, and every census from 1990 to 2020 counted more people than the last.

The 2020 census counted 11,859 housing units, 5.6 percent of them empty.

The Troy Historic District

The older core is distinctive. Overfield Tavern, from 1808, is now a museum, and the Troy-Hayner Cultural Center fills a 1914 Romanesque mansion. The Hobart Welded Steel House Company built just 22 prefabricated steel houses, every one in Troy, and 16 survive on the National Register of Historic Places.

The Historic District is an overlay running roughly from the Miami River on the north to Canal Street on the south, and from Oxford Street on the west to Clay Street on the east. The Planning Commission reviews alterations there, so check before you repaint, reside or replace windows for a sale.

Which school district is the house in?

Most of Troy belongs to Troy City Schools. A slice of the city falls in the Miami East Local School District, so verify the district for your exact address before you advertise it. Buyers with children will ask.

Property maintenance and zoning

The city enforces the International Property Maintenance Code on existing homes and other structures, and ignoring it can bring penalties from the courts. Property maintenance staff log complaints and also spot problems on their own. Troy publishes an exterior checklist. Walk your property with it before you list to catch peeling paint, broken steps or overgrown yards.

If you added a shed, deck, garage or pool, ask the city's Planning and Zoning Division whether the zoning permit was finished. A buyer's inspector or lender may ask for the paper trail.

Water service lines and utility transfer

Troy houses built before February 1, 1944 could have lead water service lines, since the city banned lead in 1944. Under the EPA's Lead and Copper Rule, the city is inventorying service line materials and mails owners of those homes a yearly letter until the line is replaced or its material is verified. A city technician can inspect in about 15 minutes on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. (937-335-4151), or you can self-report online.

For the buyer, the Utility Billing office at City Hall, 100 S. Market Street, opens service with photo ID plus a deed, closing papers or an accepted purchase contract. Any delinquency must be cleared first. Settle your own account and call the office about the handover.

Deed transfer through Miami County

Standards Miami County adopted on August 12, 2025 set the sequence. The Engineer's office approves the instrument first. The Auditor then takes a completed DTE 100 statement of value or a DTE 100 EX exemption form. The Recorder files a deed only after it carries both approval stamps.

  • Seller names on the deed must match the previous deed, or an affidavit under Ohio Revised Code 5301.252 has to explain the gap in title.
  • A land contract needs Engineer approval and an Auditor date stamp before it is recorded.
  • Fee checks go to the Miami County Auditor for the exact amount, because overpayments are refused.
  • The Auditor's website has a conveyance fee calculator that adds in the parcel transfer fee.

Ohio Revised Code 322.02 puts the county transfer tax on the grantor. The same standards cover next-of-kin affidavits, survivorship transfers and transfer on death affidavits, which helps when a Troy house comes from an estate.

When a direct sale suits a Troy house

Three kinds of Troy property tend to fit. One is a pre-1944 house with an unverified water line and old systems. Another is a rental, since about 34.5 percent of occupied Troy homes aren't owner-occupied. The third is an estate house where the heirs live elsewhere.

In each case, ask the buyer in writing who handles the lead line inventory, any open permit and the county transfer paperwork. Keep a copy of the signed purchase contract for the utility office.

Disclosure form timing

Under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30, a buyer who first sees the property disclosure form after signing may rescind in writing within three business days of receipt. That right ends 30 days after acceptance or at closing, whichever is earlier. A buyer who received the form before making an offer has no rescission right.

Hand over the form with the first showing packet. A seller who inherited the house and did not live in it during the prior year is exempt.

A practical order of steps

Start with the house itself. Find out whether it sits in the Historic District, whether it predates 1944, and whether any shed, deck or pool lacks a finished permit. Those three answers drive most of what comes later, and each one is a single call to the city.

Next, gather the paperwork. Pull the previous deed so the seller names match, and decide whether an affidavit is needed. Ask your attorney or title company for the DTE 100 or DTE 100 EX and run your price through the Auditor's calculator so there are no surprises on closing day.

Last, plan the handover. The buyer will need photo ID and the closing papers at the Utility Billing office, and you'll want your own account settled. Whether the buyer pays cash or uses a loan, these steps stay the same. A cash buyer simply removes the loan approval and appraisal wait from the schedule.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I file a deed for a Troy house?

Miami County handles it. The Engineer approves the description, the Auditor processes the conveyance form, and the Recorder files the deed. Begin with the Engineer.

Does Troy have a historic district that limits changes?

Inside the overlay, yes: the Planning Commission reviews alterations. The district is generally bounded by the Miami River, Clay, Canal and Oxford streets, and Planning and Zoning can tell you if your address is in it.

Will an old Troy home need a lead service line inspection?

Only homes built before February 1, 1944 are in the inventory. Those owners receive a yearly letter until the line is replaced or its material is confirmed by inspection or self-report.

Who pays the conveyance fee when a Troy house sells?

You do, as grantor, under Ohio Revised Code 322.02. Run your sale price through the Miami County Auditor's online calculator, which includes the parcel transfer fee, before the closing date.

Can I sell a Troy house with unpermitted work?

Yes, though a buyer's inspector may ask about permits. Check with Planning and Zoning on any shed, deck or pool, and document or correct it before you list.

Selling a house in Wooster

Wooster is a Wayne County city of 27,115 people, named for Revolutionary War general David Wooster. Population has barely moved in fifteen years: 26,119 in 2010, 27,232 at the 2020 census and 27,115 now. The College of Wooster and two Ohio State campuses share the city, and the local job base is broad, which keeps demand for older houses near downtown steady.

Public schools belong to the Wooster City School District. Confirm which building serves your address before you list, since buyers with children will ask.

The Wooster housing market

The typical Wooster home is valued at $214,200 and the typical monthly rent is $918, against a household income of $66,898. Owners live in 65.2% of the homes. Prices here sit well above those in many Ohio cities of similar size, so a seller is working in a firmer price band.

  • Wooster counts 11,108 households of 2.11 people each, and 37.3% of them were one person living alone in 2020.
  • About one resident in five (20.9%) is past 65, so estate and downsizing sales are a routine part of the market.
  • The average trip to work takes 17.4 minutes.

Short commutes and a college-town feel help older houses near downtown, but they don't hide deferred maintenance. A buyer who needs a mortgage brings in an appraiser and an inspector, and either can reopen the price. Some owners skip that step by taking an as-is offer.

Property code enforcement

The city's Building Standards Division enforces the property maintenance and zoning codes on existing buildings, through complaints plus systematic inspections of older neighborhoods. It completes more than 1,000 inspections a year. Complaint-driven inspections find a violation about 80% of the time, while the targeted sweeps find one about 20% of the time.

When a violation is confirmed, an inspector contacts the owner and mails a letter, because the city deals with owners rather than tenants. If the issue isn't resolved, the city can mow, haul debris or hire a contractor and then assess the cost to the owner, or refer the case for prosecution. About 5 to 10 houses are demolished in Wooster in an average year.

These are the most common violations, and each is cheaper to fix before showings than after a buyer's inspector writes it up:

  • Weeds or grass above twelve inches (International Property Maintenance Code 302.4).
  • Rubbish or garbage piled outside or inside the structure (code 308.1).
  • Vehicles parked on lawns, tree lawns or sidewalks (Wooster Codified Ordinance 1169.10).
  • Peeling or flaking paint and unprotected exterior wood (code 304.2).
  • Roofs that admit rain and gutters or downspouts in poor repair (code 304.7).
  • Unlicensed or inoperable vehicles stored on the lot (code 302.8).
  • Cracked or broken window glass (code 304.13.1) and unsound decks or porches (code 304.10).

Permits, plan review and code complaints run through the city's online OpenGov system, used for paperless permitting since 2017.

Wayne County value appeals

Valuation belongs to the Wayne County Auditor, whose office is at 428 West Liberty Street in Wooster, and collection belongs to the treasurer. An owner who disputes the value files a complaint with the Board of Revision between January 1 and March 31 for the tax year just ended. Mailed complaints must be postmarked by March 31, and email or fax filings must arrive by 11:59 p.m. that day.

A few rules matter if a sale is close:

  • The complaint must be signed and notarized (Ohio Revised Code 5715.13).
  • An owner may file only one complaint per three-year cycle unless certain conditions are met. The current cycle covers tax years 2026, 2027 and 2028.
  • You still owe the first-half bill, and the second-half bill isn't mailed until the complaint is resolved. If the board changes the value, any over- or underpayment is adjusted on the second-half bill.
  • Auditor staff can't give legal advice, so consider an attorney for a complaint tied to a pending sale.

Before fixing a closing date, ask the treasurer's office what is owed on your parcel. The title company needs that figure to split the bill between you and the buyer.

Farmland and large lots

Wooster is still an agricultural center, and some parcels around it may be enrolled in the Current Agricultural Use Value (CAUV) program, which lowers the tax bill on land kept in farm use. When land leaves agricultural use, Ohio Revised Code 5713.34 recoups the tax savings from the three tax years before the conversion and records the charge as a lien on the land.

The deed process asks about this too. Ohio Revised Code 319.202 builds a question into the deed paperwork. The buyer's value statement must either affirm that the seller said the land wasn't in the program or attach a sworn instrument saying it was, and only then does the auditor endorse the deed. If you're selling a house on several acres, call the Wayne County Auditor at (330) 287-5430 and ask whether the parcel is enrolled in CAUV or in an agricultural district, which runs for five years and carries a penalty for early withdrawal.

Who handles each step

Most steps run through the city's Building Standards Division, the county auditor and the board of revision.

Showing a Wooster house

Wooster Memorial Park, known locally as Spangler Park, has about seven miles of trails along Rathburn Run, and Freedlander Park holds the city pool, basketball courts and a pond. If your listing is near a park or the college, say so in the first lines of the description.

When a cash offer makes sense

Consider a cash offer if speed or condition outweighs the last dollar of list price. A Wooster listing means open houses, an inspection report and a lender's appraisal, and a violation letter from the city or a tired roof can stall each of them.

A direct purchase leaves the repairs to the buyer, which fits an inherited property, a rental with tenant trouble or a home with an open Building Standards case. Put every offer side by side, including who covers closing costs and the exact closing day, and read the settlement statement before you sign.

An order of steps for a quick sale

Start with the lot. Mow, clear rubbish and move parked vehicles off the lawn, then walk the exterior for peeling paint, gutters and broken glass. Those are the items inspectors write up most, and a clean exterior makes a better first impression anyway.

Next, call the treasurer's office to learn what is owed on the parcel, and ask the auditor whether the land is in CAUV. Then line up a title company, which carries the paperwork through the auditor's endorsement and the recorder's filing.

Finally, decide on your buyer. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is removes the appraisal and repair negotiation, but the county steps stay the same. Whoever buys, get the closing date and cost split in writing.

Can I sell a Wooster house that has an open code violation?

Yes, but disclose it to every buyer. Building Standards will agree on a workable timeline if an owner shows a plan, and cases left unresolved are referred for prosecution. Many owners clear the violation before closing.

When can I appeal my Wayne County property value?

The window opens January 1 and closes March 31, and it covers the tax year just ended. For tax year 2026 that means January 1 through March 31, 2027. Expect a notary step and a limit of one complaint per three-year cycle.

Do I need a disclosure form for an inherited house in Wooster?

Often no. The statute excuses an estate's fiduciary and an heir who did not live in the house during the prior year. An heir who did live there should plan to complete the form.

What happens if my parcel is in the CAUV farm program?

A change away from farm use brings a charge equal to the savings over the three prior tax years (ORC 5713.34). Call the Wayne County Auditor before signing, so the contract says who pays it.

Who records the deed after a Wooster sale?

The Wayne County recorder files it after a notary or another listed official has taken the owner's acknowledgment and the auditor has endorsed the conveyance. The title company usually carries the paperwork through each step.

How the Lake Erie shoreline changes a sale

Avon Lake fronts Lake Erie on the north edge of Lorain County, roughly 17 miles from Cleveland, and a lakefront or bluff-top house can fall under state erosion rules that never touch an inland one. Learn which side of that line your parcel is on before you name a price.

The city has an estimated 26,486 people, up from 25,204 in April 2020, and covers 11.13 square miles. It grew fast through the late twentieth century, and many houses now change hands after long ownership.

Avon Lake homes in brief

Owners dominate here. In 2020 to 2024 data, 83.1% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the median value is $368,300. Avon Lake has 10,896 households averaging 2.35 people. A homeowner with a mortgage pays a median of $1,949 a month in owner costs, a homeowner without one pays $849, and the median renter pays $1,537.

Long tenure means many sales come from a move toward family, a smaller home, or an inherited house that needs work. A seller who wants to close quickly has to pick between fixing the house first and selling it as is.

Lake Erie erosion and your disclosure form

It matters if the parcel lies inside a state-designated Coastal Erosion Area. The Ohio Department of Natural Resources requires land in such an area to be named on the state residential disclosure form when it sells, and a CEA permit comes first for a new building, a septic system, or a ground-level addition of 500 square feet or more.

The state's map viewer takes an address search. A heavy red line marks the landward edge of the area, and a data table lists measured recession in feet per year and the distance expected over the next 30 years if no further erosion control is added. Owners inside a designated area in Lorain, Erie, Ottawa or Lucas County may also qualify for the Erosion Control Loan Program.

Before listing a shoreline house, run its address through the viewer. If it falls inside the line, say so on the form and expect questions about shoreline work, past repairs and permits.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Avon Lake house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Building permits and short-term rentals

The Avon Lake Building Department issues permits for buildings and structures, does the inspections tied to each permit, and enforces the Ohio Building Code and the Residential Code of Ohio. The online portal takes applications, and the office sits at 750 Avon Belden Road. Close out any permit with unfinished work before listing, because buyers' inspectors look for it. Office hours are weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and a drop box at the entrance takes paperwork after hours and is emptied each weekday morning, which helps if you are finishing a permit while managing a move.

Vacation-style rentals get a separate program. Under Ordinance 25-161 an owner applies for certification, the city sends someone for a life safety inspection within 14 days, and the certificate lasts 12 months before renewal. The application asks for proof of insurance and of paid property taxes and utilities. Chapter 14 also keeps short-term rentals 1,000 feet apart, with a carve-out for properties already operating before the ordinance.

A house that has hosted short-term guests raises one question for Community Development: does the certificate pass to a buyer? Anyone planning to keep renting will want the answer before closing.

Deeds and tax bills at Lorain County offices

An Avon Lake deed is transferred at the Lorain County Auditor's office in Elyria. Conveyances arrive in person or through an approved e-file vendor, and mail is not accepted. Handwritten forms are refused, anything incomplete or short on fees is returned, and staff may not advise on the forms. A title company or attorney usually does the filing.

Because the state can change the schedule, ask the treasurer's office which dates govern the year you close. On the deed itself, ORC 5301.01 calls for the seller's signature to be acknowledged before a notary or similar official, and ORC 5301.25 makes recording with the county recorder the buyer's shield against later claims.

Cash offer or listing?

A listing can pay the most when the house shows well and you can sit through showings and an appraisal. A cash offer swaps some of that price for a fixed closing date and no dependence on a buyer's mortgage approval.

Whichever route you lean toward, have each buyer put the price, the closing date and the split of title and transfer costs on paper. Fill in the disclosure form early, with shoreline notes if they apply, and confirm no permit is open. Then set each offer next to a listing's likely net, after agent fees, repairs and the carrying costs of the weeks it takes.

The disclosure form and the three-day window

Ohio law has the seller of a residence with up to four units complete the state disclosure form (ORC 5302.30). If the form reaches the buyer after the contract is signed, the buyer may cancel in writing within three business days, so hand it over with the first offer. For a lakefront or bluff-top house, add what you know about shoreline work, repairs and permits. A short, complete form builds trust with a cash buyer and shortens the back-and-forth after an inspection.

Getting ready before you accept an offer

A few steps save trouble later. Check the erosion map for your address. Ask the Building Department whether every permit is closed. If the house was a short-term rental, ask Community Development about the certificate. Ask the treasurer for the tax balance and the due dates that apply to your closing year. Then let the title company handle the notary, the auditor in Elyria and the recording, so the deed reaches the right office complete and typed. Keep copies of the signed disclosure form and the contract.

Frequently asked questions

Is my Avon Lake house in a Coastal Erosion Area?

Search the address in the ODNR Coastal Erosion Area map viewer. Property inside the area is named on the state disclosure form at sale, and a new building, a septic system or an addition of 500 square feet or more needs a CEA permit.

Does an Avon Lake seller have to fill out the state disclosure form?

Most do. ORC 5302.30 covers homes of up to four units, and it excepts estate fiduciaries, transfers to relatives and sales to a buyer who already lived there for a year.

Can a buyer keep running my Avon Lake short-term rental?

Ask the city first. Ordinance 25-161 certifies each short-term rental after an application and a life safety inspection, renewed every 12 months, so whether a new owner inherits the certificate is a question for Community Development.

How does a deed get filed with Lorain County?

Through the Lorain County Auditor in Elyria, in person or by e-file, with no mail accepted and every form typed and complete. A title company normally takes care of it at closing.

When are Lorain County property taxes due?

Selling a house in Xenia

Xenia is the Greene County seat, about 15 miles east of Dayton in the Miami Valley, and storms shaped its housing history. An F5 tornado crossed the middle of the city on April 3, 1974, killing 34 people and destroying almost half of the city's buildings. Another tornado, rated F4, hit on September 20, 2000. The city keeps a system of tornado sirens.

A seller who can hand a buyer receipts for a recent roof, siding or storm repair has useful paperwork, because storm history is an obvious question in Xenia.

Xenia housing numbers

The market sits between a college-town market and a heavily rental city. Population is an estimated 26,425, a 3.8% gain on the 25,447 counted in 2020. Figures for 2020 to 2024 follow.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 60.9%, with a median owner-occupied value of $162,400.
  • Median gross rent: $931.
  • 10,765 households averaging 2.32 people.
  • 22.4% of residents are under 18, and 20.4% are 65 or older.
  • Mean travel time to work is 24.6 minutes, and the city's website carries a page for people relocating to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.
  • Median household income is $56,029.

Xenia sits in a transportation triangle formed by I-70, I-71 and I-75, reached by U.S. 35, U.S. 42 and U.S. 68. A listing can state the highway access plainly, since buyers who drive to Dayton or beyond will check it.

Schools and neighborhood draws

Xenia Community Schools serves the city, and private options include Legacy Christian Academy and St. Brigid School. Confirm which building serves your address before you list.

The Little Miami Scenic Trail runs through Xenia Station, and the city carries the nickname "Bicycle Capital of the Midwest," since five of its six former rail roadbeds have been converted to trail use. The Greene County Fairgrounds hosts the annual Dayton Hamvention, which typically draws more than 20,000 amateur radio enthusiasts. If your house sits near the fairgrounds, mention the event traffic in your showing notes so buyers aren't surprised.

Zoning and property maintenance rules

Planning and Zoning issues zoning permits and also enforces the property maintenance code, the city's floor for safe, sanitary buildings. The division works from the City Administration Building at 107 East Main Street, weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m., and takes calls at 937-372-6389.

Two practical points for sellers:

  • The city's project list includes a "Zoning Update 2026." Ask Planning and Zoning whether the update changes the rules for your lot, an addition or an accessory building before you promise a buyer a particular use.
  • Code enforcement is separate from the Building Division. Answer a notice about tall grass, debris or a failing structure before the house goes on the market.

Planning and Zoning sits under the Development Services Department, the place to start with a question about an unpermitted porch, deck or garage.

How Greene County values a house and when you can appeal

The Greene County Auditor values property by mass appraisal, building a table from sales data in each area and testing it against actual sales. Ohio doesn't allow foreclosure sales in that analysis because they aren't arm's-length sales, so a distressed sale next door shouldn't drag your value down in the county's model.

A triennial update happens every three years without a visual inspection, and a full revaluation with a physical review happens in the sixth year. An owner who thinks the appraisal is too high may file with the Greene County Board of Revision, and the window runs January 1 to March 31. There's no dollar-for-dollar link between a change in value and a change in taxes, because the voted levies are applied to the value.

Homestead rules and income limits change over time, so ask the Greene County Auditor for the current application and limits.

Tax relief after a tornado or fire

Ohio Revised Code 323.17 gives the county board of revision a specific tool. If fire, flood, a tornado or another cause destroys or damages taxable property by 25% or more of its listed value, and at least $2,000 of taxable value, the board may pass a resolution pushing the payment deadline back by as much as a year.

Copies go to the auditor and treasurer along with the board's damage estimate. Owners selling a storm-damaged house should ask the Greene County Auditor how to request an extension and tell the title company, so the settlement statement shows what remains unpaid.

Deed, recording and transfer fee

Three offices touch a Xenia deed. A notary or another listed official takes the owner's acknowledgment (ORC 5301.01), the Greene County Auditor endorses the conveyance once the buyer files a value statement and the seller pays the conveyance fee (ORC 319.202), and the recorder then files it. A deed left unrecorded can lose to a later buyer who had no notice (ORC 5301.25).

A cash offer suits a Xenia house that a lender's appraiser would mark down, such as one with worn shingles, a wet basement or storm repairs never finished. Owners who inherited a house or manage a rental from out of town also use it.

Get each offer in writing with the closing date and the party responsible for closing costs. Set the figures beside what a regular listing would net after commission and repairs, and ask the title company for a draft settlement statement early.

A practical order for a quick sale

Begin with the paperwork on the house. Gather receipts for roof, siding and storm repairs, and check with Planning and Zoning about any porch, deck or garage built without a permit. Clear any notice about grass, debris or a failing structure.

Then line up the deed. Find a notary, plan for the value statement the buyer files with the auditor, and budget for the conveyance fee, which is the seller's cost. Ask the title company to prepare the settlement statement early so you can see what remains unpaid, especially if a tornado or fire damaged the house and a tax extension is in play.

A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal and any repair demands, which helps when a house needs work. The county steps stay the same for every kind of sale, and a deed that isn't recorded promptly can lose out to a later buyer.

Does Xenia's tornado history change how I should sell?

It changes what buyers ask. The April 1974 F5 and the September 2000 F4 are well known, so keep receipts for roof, siding and storm repairs and hand them over early. The city also keeps a siren system, which some buyers ask about.

Does Greene County count a foreclosure sale when it sets values?

No. Ohio doesn't allow foreclosure sales in the county's analysis because they aren't arm's-length sales. Ordinary sales in your area are what the appraisal tables are tested against.

Is my Xenia house covered by a tax extension if a tornado damaged it?

Possibly. Section 323.17 lets the Greene County board of revision grant up to a year more to pay when the loss reaches 25% of listed value and $2,000 of taxable value. Ask the auditor how to apply.

Where do I ask about zoning for a house in Xenia?

Phone Planning and Zoning at 937-372-6389 or stop by 107 East Main Street on a weekday between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. Raise the Zoning Update 2026 project if the property has an addition or a second building.

How long can I wait to appeal my Greene County value?

The county takes complaints from January 1 until March 31 each year. The board looks at value only, so the voted levy rates stay as they are.

Land area is 11.58 square miles, so lots near the Square are tight.

Historic homes near the Square

Medina's center is a historic district, so older homes near the Square sit in a place that works to preserve its look. A Community Design Committee and a Historic Preservation Board look after the historic character, and the district covers a nine-block area around Uptown Park.

The Square dates to rebuilding after two fires. An 1848 blaze destroyed the whole business district, and an 1870 fire destroyed 45 buildings. It took almost ten years to replace them, which is why Victorian style is so common there. Medina was founded in 1818 and chartered as a city in 1952.

For a house in or near the district, check with the city on whether exterior work needs review, and do that before promising a buyer any changes.

The Medina City School District serves the city. Its schools include Medina High School, A.I. Root and Claggett middle schools, and the elementary schools Ella Canavan, H.G. Blake, Sidney Fenn, Eliza Northrop and Ralph E. Waite. Garfield and Heritage elementary schools closed at the end of the 2023-24 school year after redistricting.

Building Department and permits

The city's Building Department handles plan review, inspections and property maintenance enforcement, and it tries to link owners of run-down properties with assistance programs and volunteer groups. You can reach it at 330-722-9030.

Ohio's 2024 Building, Mechanical and Plumbing Codes took effect March 1, 2024, and the department holds every application received after that date to those requirements. Ask the city's Planning Department any zoning questions about a lot or an outbuilding.

  • Sales to cover delinquent taxes or assessments.

An exempt transfer still needs paperwork. Ohio Revised Code 319.202 swaps the full value statement for a short statement of the exemption reason.

Selling a Medina rental

A rental parcel needs a contact filing at the county auditor, with updates due 60 days after any change (Ohio Revised Code 5323.02). The auditor's endorsement on a rental deed points the new owner to that filing.

Bring up the tenants and the lease in your first talk with a buyer. Keep records of deposits and rent already paid, and agree in writing who returns deposits and when tenants must move out.

From signed contract to recorded deed

Once you have a signed contract, ask a title company or attorney to prepare the deed, and order a payoff letter if you owe on a mortgage. Usually not. The county exempts transfers to an heir or devisee and among heirs when no money is paid. The buyer or recipient still files the exemption statement, DTE 100EX.

Do I have to give a buyer Ohio's disclosure form?

Yes for houses of one to four units, subject to exceptions. A buyer who gets it after the contract is signed has three business days to rescind (Ohio Revised Code 5302.30).

Why does Medina Square have so many Victorian buildings?

The business district was destroyed by fire in 1848, and a second fire in 1870 destroyed 45 buildings. Rebuilding took almost ten years, and the Square is now a recognized historic district.

The Lorain County Treasurer runs an optional monthly escrow plan for tax payments, and the treasurer's site posts the current due dates, which have moved when the state changed the schedule. Your title company will prorate the tax between you and the buyer.

Rules that affect a house you plan to sell

The Avon Building and Zoning Departments share City Hall at 36600 Detroit Road. Contact the Building Department about a pool, irrigation, deck, patio, shed, finished basement, fence, new roof, siding or any addition, and note that contractors must be registered. Check that each of those projects at your house has a closed permit.

  • Utilities: water and sewer bills go out monthly and are due on the 25th, and meters report actual daily use. Call the Utilities Department to move service out of your name.
  • Sprinklers: an in-ground system needs an approved backflow device, tested each year before June 30, with results sent to the city.
  • Short-term rentals: a 2021 ordinance extending a moratorium treats any use missing from the zoning code as barred, and short-term rentals are missing from it. Ask the Zoning Department whether anything has changed before you market the house to an investor.

Avon also keeps a Do Not Knock list, and an address stays registered for three years. A seller who is tired of unsolicited offers can ask the city about it.
